patients.label: Man in his 70s with pacemaker lead endocarditis

identity_evidence.quote: The patient was a male in his 70s

attribution_limitations: Blood culture reporting differs between sections: the body says three sets initially yielded negative results and that repeated cultures were positive for Staphylococcus epidermidis, while the abstract says three sets were subsequently positive for coagulase-negative Staphylococcus epidermidis after the empirical antibiotics were discontinued. The source does not state how many sets were positive.

The triple antibiotic regimen names only vancomycin and gentamicin; flucloxacillin and rifampicin were prescribed later after sensitivity testing. Vancomycin is said to be discontinued after sensitivity testing, yet a four-week vancomycin course is described after pacemaker removal.
The patient is said to have no interaction with farm or domesticated animals yet owns a pet dog.

The source gives no explicit link that the discontinued empirical antibiotic regimen in the abstract is the piperacillin with tazobactam given on presentation, and no dates, doses or durations for the antibiotics.
The abstract says the pacemaker infection occurred long after installation, while the case text says the pacemaker was replaced a year ago; the original implantation date is not given.

claims.text: A man in his 70s with a pacemaker placed for 2:1 heart block and replaced a year earlier, glaucoma, hypertension and recurrent epididymitis, living with his spouse and owning a pet dog (yet described as having no interaction with farm or domesticated animals), had three months of cold and shivering episodes (rigors) two to three times a week with subsequent excessive heat and temperature rise to 38 degrees Celsius. There were no reported loss of consciousness, tongue biting, eye-rolling or incontinence episodes. He had received two courses of oral antibiotics from his general practitioner and then intravenous piperacillin with tazobactam on presentation.

claims.text: He was treated on admission for an infection of unknown origin. Workup showed leucocytosis with neutrophilia, fluctuating raised C-reactive protein, initially negative blood cultures, normal urine microscopy, negative urine nitrite, negative respiratory PCR for respiratory syncytial virus and COVID-19, a paced rhythm on ECG, negative infectious serologies, unremarkable chest X-rays and CT of thorax, abdomen and pelvis, and normal transthoracic echocardiography. After the intravenous antibiotics were discontinued, blood cultures grew coagulase-negative Staphylococcus epidermidis, and transoesophageal echocardiography showed echogenic shadowing of at least 2.5 by 1.3 cm on the right ventricular pacing lead with vegetation, consistent with a likely endocarditis of the ventricular pacing lead.
